Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.2 Nonverbal Cues
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 3.1.2 Nonverbal Cues, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do non- verbal cues enhance communication? 2. Why should we articulate vowel sounds correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a video recording and pick out words featuring the sounds /ᴧ / / æ / /aʊ / /əʊ/ /w/ /j/. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light.
2. work with peers and practise minimal pairs such as hut and hat; 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 3.1.2 Nonverbal Cues together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn as the learner acquires the skill of organising their own knowledge as they role play a conversation

and use nonverbal cues such as facial expressions, gestures, eye contact and body movement.

● Critical thinking and Problem solving as the learner records themself and exchange the recordings and give feedback

Values:
● Respect is promoted as the learner appreciates diverse opinions as they watch video clips and identify nonverbal cues

such as dress choice, personal space and body movement among others.

● Peace is promoted as the learner displays calmness as they brainstorm various non-verbal cues.
